question.text: A corporate bond or debenture issued through a public offering in India must be:

answer.text: Guaranteed by the Reserve Bank of India
Listed only on BSE, not NSE
Rated by one or more independent credit rating agencies
Converted to equity shares within five years

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that corporate debentures and bonds are rated by independent credit rating agencies, especially when they are issued through public offerings. The rating gives prospective investors an independent assessment of the issuer's creditworthiness. The Trap: "Guaranteed by RBI" is wrong because RBI does not guarantee corporate bonds. "Listed only on BSE" is wrong because bonds can be listed on either exchange. "Converted to equity" describes convertible debentures, not all corporate bonds. Note: A credit rating is an opinion on credit quality, not a guarantee of repayment. Even highly rated bonds can be downgraded over time, and clients should understand that rating actions do happen during the life of an instrument.
